{{Short description|Theorem on prime factors}}
In [[number theory]], the '''Erdős arcsine law''', named after [[Paul Erdős]] in 1969,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Manstavičius |first=E. |title=Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics |chapter-url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783112319321-032/html |chapter=A proof of the Erdös arcsine law |date=2020-05-18 |pages=533–564 |publisher=De Gruyter |isbn=978-3-11-231932-1 |language=en |doi=10.1515/9783112319321-032}}</ref> states that the [[prime number|prime]] [[divisor]]s of a number have a [[Distribution (mathematics)|distribution]] related to the [[arcsine distribution]].

Specifically, say that the {{mvar|j}}<sup>th</sup> prime factor {{mvar|p}} of a given number {{mvar|n}} (in the sorted sequence of distinct prime factors) is "small" when {{math|1=log(log(''p'')) < ''j''}}.  Then, for any fixed parameter {{mvar|u}}, in the limit as {{mvar|x}} goes to infinity, the proportion of the integers {{mvar|n}} less than {{mvar|x}} that have fewer than {{math|1=''u'' log(log(''n''))}} small prime factors converges to

: <math> \frac{2}{\pi} \arcsin{ \sqrt{u} }. </math>
